## Design roles

Each part does a job for the person. These are the jobs, as questions the part answers.

<div class="odv-am-rolelist"><span class="odv-am-role big"><b>Containment</b> What holds this?</span><span class="odv-am-role big"><b>Layering</b> What sits on top?</span><span class="odv-am-role big"><b>Hierarchy</b> What do you read first?</span><span class="odv-am-role big"><b>Readability</b> Can you read it?</span><span class="odv-am-role big"><b>Emphasis</b> Where does the eye go?</span><span class="odv-am-role big"><b>Meaning</b> What state is it in?</span><span class="odv-am-role big"><b>Affordance</b> Can you act on it?</span><span class="odv-am-role big"><b>Feedback</b> Did it respond?</span><span class="odv-am-role big"><b>Focus</b> Where is the keyboard?</span><span class="odv-am-role big"><b>Grouping</b> What belongs together?</span><span class="odv-am-role big"><b>Reach</b> Can you hit it?</span></div>

## How the decisions reach each part

Each part follows a chain: an answer about the product, the rule it set, the token that carries it, and the value you see. The numbers match the drawing.

title="What sits on top?">Layering</span></header><ul class="odv-am-tree"><li><b class="odv-am-lbl">Answer</b><div class="odv-am-main">Elevation · What rises above the page? → Only what floats</div><div class="odv-am-why">Only menus and dialogs float.</div></li><li><b class="odv-am-lbl">Answer</b><div class="odv-am-main">Elevation · How soft are shadows? → Soft</div><div class="odv-am-why">Soft shadows suit warm paper.</div></li><li><b class="odv-am-lbl">Rule</b><div class="odv-am-main">For a menu or dialog, use elevation.overlay and a dimmed page. Don't use no shadow.</div><div class="odv-am-why">The dimmed page focuses the reader on the dialog.</div></li><li><b class="odv-am-lbl">Token</b><div class="odv-am-chain"><code>color.surface.raised</code><span>→</span><code>overlay.background</code><span class="odv-am-val">#FFFFFF · dark #1F1B16</span><span class="odv-byscheme" title="Its value changes by scheme. Changing this pick moves only what reads color.surface.raised.</div></div></li><li><b class="odv-am-lbl">Token</b><div class="odv-am-chain"><code>elevation.overlay</code><span>→</span><code>overlay.shadow</code><span class="odv-am-val">0px 12px 32px, #1F1B1629 · dark 0px 12px 32px, #00000080</span><span class="odv-byscheme" title="Its value changes by scheme. <section class="odv-am-card" id="part-7"><div class="odv-am-img"><div class="odv-am-menu part"><div class="odv-am-row is-highlight"><svg class="odv-am-icon" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true"><rect width="14" height="14" x="8" y="8" rx="2" ry="2"/><path d="M4 16c-1.1 0-2-.9-2-2V4c0-1.1.9-2 2-2h10c1.1 0 2 .9 2 2"/></svg><span class="odv-am-label">Copy</span><span class="odv-am-fill"></span><span class="odv-am-key">⌘C</span><i class="odv-am-n">7</i></div></div></div><div class="odv-am-body"><header><i class="odv-am-n">7</i><b>Highlight fill</b><span class="odv-am-role" title="Did it respond?">Feedback</span></header><ul class="odv-am-tree"><li><b class="odv-am-lbl">Answer</b><div class="odv-am-main">Accessibility · Which states get their own visible value? → Those and pressed</div><div class="odv-am-why">Pressed gets its own value for touch.</div></li><li><b class="odv-am-lbl">Answer</b><div class="odv-am-main">Motion · How fast does feedback feel? → Moderate</div><div class="odv-am-why">Moderate speed feels calm.</div></li><li><b class="odv-am-lbl">Rule</b><div class="odv-am-main">For hover and press feedback, use motion.duration.feedback (moderate). A fast flash feels jumpy.</div></li><li><b class="odv-am-lbl">Token</b><div class="odv-am-chain"><code>color.surface.highlight</code><span>→</span><code>item.background.highlight</code><span class="odv-am-val">#F6F2EA · dark #2E2A24</span><span class="odv-byscheme" title="Its value changes by scheme. The part is the same in every scheme."><svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" width="11" height="11" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m11 10 3 3"/><path d="M6.5 21A3.5 3.5 0 1 0 3 17.5a2.62 2.62 0 0 1-.708 1.792A1 1 0 0 0 3 21z"/><path d="M9.969 17.031 21.378 5.624a1 1 0 0 0-3.002-3.002L6.967 14.031"/></svg>By scheme</span></div><div class="odv-am-why">The fill of the item the pointer or the keyboard is on, or whose submenu is open. A state shows on the item's background, one step from the surface it sits on: darker in light, lighter in dark.</div><div class="odv-am-lines"><div><b>Pick</b> neutral.100, two steps darker than the surfaces it sits on (neutral.0), so the item under the pointer or the keyboard reads as a band without lifting off the page. It skips neutral.50, the page canvas, so a menu item never matches the page behind it.</div><div><b>Dark</b> neutral.100, one step lighter than the surfaces it sits on (neutral.50), so the item under the pointer or the keyboard reads as a band on the menu and on cards.</div><div><b>Shares the step with</b> surface.sunken, action.secondary.hover, category.5.subtle, disabled.surface. Changing this pick moves only what reads color.surface.highlight.</div></div></li></ul></div></section>

## For agents

Agents get this same anatomy: every part, its roles, whether it is required, the tokens it reads and the decisions behind them.

- **From an AI agent:** call the `get_anatomy` tool on the Open DS MCP server, with this scheme and `dropdown-menu`.
- **From a terminal:** `npx open-ds anatomy content-first dropdown-menu`
